name: Cards From Files
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Give any consumer cards for the knowledge it already keeps in files, so recall starts from what is there instead of an empty store.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (the card store does) and choosing which cards a task sees (the context assembler does).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the mixed pinned cases is at least that of every free topic builder, with a store far below one card per file (metric-cards-from-files).
knowledge: Code graphs and repository maps group code by its call and import structure without a model; topic cards a model writes add the names a person would search for. A card groups information on one topic from many files and sources; a card per file is an index of files, so per_file_symbols and the degenerate groupings are baselines for file finding and never builders to ship. The earlier selection of per_file_symbols came from the file-finding metric, whose cases have one needed file each and so favour a card per file by construction; that metric alone was ill-posed for this solution. Its cases are now one kind of a mixed set with topic cases and a store-size term, and the selection is back on llm_topic_cards until that one number decides.
measures_of_success: The files a piece of work needed are inside the first cards the fixed selector picks, with little noise and with files of more than one folder bundled when the task spans them, from a store of at most 0.25 cards per file, at a price per build a team would pay.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score. The per-file builder is a baseline for finding one file, not a card builder. The free topic builders (cochange_topic_cards, import_graph_topic_cards, the replay of the saved paid build) are scored for free; docs/how-to/iterate-on-card-builders-without-repeating-model-calls.md says how to iterate before any paid run.

name: Acting
description: Takes a goal with a written done-standard and tries to bring it about outside the model, by editing files, calling a write operation or running an agent, then reports whether the goal was met.
purpose: Make intended changes in the world and no unrequested ones, for any product that lets an AI act.
approach: Attempt the goal inside a bounded workspace, check it against its done-standard and report the result.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-act-in-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Intended changes made, no unrequested ones.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: A goal with a written done-standard, and a brief.
outputs: A DeepResult that says whether the goal was met, with the reason; it never raises.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Nervous System
description: Watches a run and raises at most one small signal when a step cannot be undone or belongs to a person, and leaves ordinary work alone. It shares one signal contract with Asking Judgment: a risk signal with a severity and a reason, which Asking Judgment turns into a decision for one person.
purpose: Stop irreversible or human-only steps before they happen, without slowing ordinary work, for any product that lets an AI act.
approach: Read a short digest of each step and signal proceed, redirect, answer now or escalate to a person.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-watch-for-risk has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-watch-for-risk has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-watch-for-risk chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Risks caught against false alarms, and latency.
parameters: The provider and model for the overseer arm, and the consumer's prompt as data.
inputs: A short digest of the run.
outputs: One signal: proceed, redirect, answer_now, escalate_deep or escalate_human; it never raises.
effects: At most one model call per step; none for the rule-based gate.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Learning
description: Names the areas whose research is older than the ninety day bar, so each can be researched again, compared and republished. The weekly research itself is run by the consumer's autopilot.
purpose: Keep every seat's candidates current for anyone who relies on the hub.
approach: Research each area again before its last research is 90 days old, compare the candidates and republish the result.
milestones: 1. Every seat's last_researched is inside the 90-day refresh window (metric-stay-current).
measures_of_success: Days since each seat was last researched and compared.
inputs: An ISO date (today when none is given).
outputs: The names of the registry's areas whose research is older than the ninety day bar on that date.
effects: Reads the registry's dated rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the weekly research is run by the consumer's autopilot.

name: Research Freshness Reader
description: Reads the date each area of the registry was last researched and reports its age against a 90 day bar, naming the stale areas.
purpose: Show maintainers which parts of the hub have gone stale.
approach: Read the recorded research dates and report the days since each.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-read-registry-freshness has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Every area's research age is read correctly.
parameters: clock: optional, so a test can fix the date.
inputs: An ISO date, or the registry facts together with a consumer's connections.
outputs: Days since the date, or the combined freshness reading with the stale areas named.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.

name: Hands
description: Broad code that makes it easy for AI to use tools, make changes in the world or get knowledge without being one specific integration. Reports how much of an area's hub connections are catalog entries that need no code, so an integration is added as data and never as code in the frontend, backend or runner.
purpose: Let users connect the apps they use with zero code per integration, for any product built on the hub.
approach: List integrations as catalog data from the hubs, connect them through one generic flow and expose their tools per user.
milestones: 1. A fake integration is added through the catalog alone and connects, calls a tool and disconnects with zero code changes. 2. At least two arms exist. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Per-integration code changes in frontend, backend and runner (target 0 each); days from a hub listing an integration to a user connecting it (target at most 7); credential isolation checks all pass.
inputs: An area name (all areas when none is named).
outputs: The share, from 0 to 1, of the area's hub connections that need only configuration.
effects: Reads the registry's connection rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty. Design: see the review page hub-integrations-zero-code.

name: Connection Scorer
description: Scores, per area, whether a hub is registered, how many of a consumer's connections need no code, and whether a fake hub is accepted by configuration alone.
purpose: Show a consumer how much of its integration is a hub connection and how much is hand-wired.
approach: Read the registry together with the consumer's binding and count connections per area.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-score-hub-connections has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Zero-code connections and hand-wired services are counted correctly.
inputs: A consumer's Binding, or one registry fact and a kind of check.
outputs: Per-area checks and a combined score.
effects: None; it reads the registry files and the consumer's declared code paths.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.

name: Card Store
description: A small store that keeps cards, the hub's own memory unit, and finds them again by words or a tag.
purpose: Keep and find cards for any consumer, with no service to run.
approach: Store each card under its id and search by every word of the query.
milestones: 1. Every case passes: cards found again by words, nothing lost on a repeated add (metric-card-store).
measures_of_success: Cards found again by words; nothing lost on a second add of the same id.
parameters: The store location (in memory or one SQLite file).
inputs: A card to add, a card id, and a query with an optional tag and a result limit.
outputs: The id of an added card, a card or nothing for an id, the cards matching a query or a tag, whether a delete removed one, and the count.
effects: Writes and deletes cards in the store (a SQLite file when one is named); reads nothing else.
usage_notes: Default arm is local SQLite, in memory or one file.

name: Internal Context
description: A system's own context made available to the AI: adapters that read its internal APIs, databases and local files, or a declaration of them. The default is local files at a standard location.
purpose: Let the AI know what a particular system knows, without the hub being written for that system.
approach: Offer one declaration for each internal source, read it through an adapter, and keep what is read as cards.
milestones: 1. An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI (metric-internal-context).
measures_of_success: An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI.
outputs: The cards of a system's own context.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.
